subject: Access handoff strategy evaluation: interface endpoint vs peering vs IPsec tunnel
messages:

Cc: neteng@evergreenbank.com
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating handoff models for Private deployment

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the earlier call. As we start a formal design review for Evergreen Bank's Private deployment, our security and network teams want a concise comparison of three handoff options: VPC peering (cross-account peering), PrivateLink / interface endpoints, and an IPsec site-to-site VPN (managed by the customer's edge).

Key Evergreen constraints:
- Data plane must never traverse public internet without encryption and must be auditable.
- Minimal changes to our existing VPC CIDR assignments (we're conservative on renumbering).
- Desire for least-privilege network surface per application team.
- SLA: ~100ms P95 for inference requests from our app tier in us-east-1.

Can your team provide a short note with tradeoffs (security, operational complexity, ongoing cost, and failure modes) and a recommendation we can present to our architects?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Network Architect
Evergreen Bank

Alex / team — attached a compact technical appendix and a handoff diagram (redwood_onramp_options_diagram.pdf). High level summary below; appendix has configuration snippets and a simple latency model.

1) VPC peering (cross-account peering)
- Security: Same network layer; no NAT required if CIDRs don't overlap. Traffic stays on the cloud provider backbone (no public internet).
- Ops: Simple to set up for single-region, single-VPC paths. Requires CIDR coordination (cannot overlap) and explicit route table updates.
- Performance: Lowest added latency (usually <1-2ms extra inside region). Good for low-latency workloads.
- Failure modes: If peering route removed or route propagation misconfigured, traffic fails silently (blackholing).
- Note for Evergreen: if you cannot renumber, peering may be ruled out for some teams.

2) PrivateLink / interface endpoint
- Security: Connects via AWS-managed ENIs in the consumer VPC; traffic is still on the backbone and can be restricted via SGs. Provides a narrower surface (per-service endpoint).
- Ops: No CIDR coordination required. Endpoint creation is straightforward; can be managed by either side (producer creates service, consumer creates endpoint).
- Performance: Small per-packet overhead vs peering (couple ms) but consistent; good SLA characteristics.
- Failure modes: Endpoint limits and ENI IP exhaustion; need to manage scaling of endpoints and SG rules.
- Note: Easier for multi-tenant customers or when strict isolation per app is required.

3) IPsec site-to-site VPN (customer-managed)
- Security: Encrypted over public internet (IKE/IPsec) — acceptable if crypto/AES is in place, but path traverses last-mile ISPs.
- Ops: Heavy day-2 burden on customer: tunnel health, key rotation, MTU issues, and NAT traversal. Also potential vendor-specific interoperability.
- Performance: Higher and more variable latency; jitter depends on ISP and routing. May struggle to hit tight P95 SLAs for inference unless you design for regional proximity and add redundant tunnels.
- Failure modes: ISP outages, asymmetric routing, and need for careful BGP or static route failover.

Recommendation (based on Evergreen constraints):
- Primary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for application-level isolation and no CIDR renumbering. Fits least-privilege surface requirement and keeps traffic on provider backbone. Add VPC Flow Logs and detailed ENI-level audit for compliance.
- Secondary / fallback: VPC peering for internal teams where CIDR coordination is feasible and you need absolute lowest latency.
- Avoid sole reliance on IPsec VPN for production inference traffic where strict latency SLOs are required; use it only as a backup or for non-latency-sensitive workloads.

Attachments: redwood_onramp_options_diagram.pdf (diagram), configuration snippets in appendix.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alex — adding the compliance checklist items Evergreen asked for. See attached evergreen_security_requirements.xlsx for the baseline items we need to satisfy before spin-up:
- KMS key ownership model and rotation windows (customer-managed preferred).
- Flow log retention and log forwarding to your SIEM (we require at least 90 days for investigations).
- IP allowlists for management ports; no management plane exposed publicly.
- SG design guidance: least-priv, ephemeral port ranges for egress, and explicit deny where applicable.

Operational asks if you pick PrivateLink:
- Ensure you have enough ENI IP capacity in the consumer subnets (we provide a sizing calc in the spreadsheet).
- Tagging and IAM role mapping for endpoint creation auditing.
- A runbook for endpoint scaling and ENI replenishment.

If you'd like, we can run a short performance proof-of-concept (week-long) with PrivateLink and a fallback peering pilot for one internal app team. That will demonstrate real P95 numbers under your traffic profile.

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

If the PoC looks good we expect to start procurement next month. Please add a brief estimate of expected monthly costs for endpoint data processing vs peering egress so procurement has a ballpark.

Appreciate it — see you on the readout.

— Alex
